SimplexCategory.comment:
The simplex category:
* objects are natural numbers `n : ℕ`
* morphisms from `n` to `m` are monotone functions `Fin (n+1) → Fin (m+1)`
SimplexCategory.description: This defines a category where objects are natural numbers and morphisms are monotone functions from the finite set of size corresponding to one natural number to that of another.

SimplexCategory.mk.comment: Interpret a natural number as an object of the simplex category.

category_theory.simplicial_object.equiva.fullDefinition: def equivalenceLeftToRight (X : SimplicialObject.Augmented C) (F : Arrow C)     (G : Augmented.toArrow.obj X ⟶ F) : X ⟶ F.augmentedCechNerve where   left :=     { app := fun x =>         Limits.WidePullback.lift (X.hom.app _ ≫ G.right)           (fun i => X.left.map (SimplexCategory.const _ x.unop i).op ≫ G.left) fun i => by           dsimp           erw [Category.assoc, Arrow.w, Augmented.toArrow_obj_hom, NatTrans.naturality_assoc,             Functor.const_obj_map, Category.id_comp]       naturality := by         intro x y f         dsimp         ext         · dsimp           simp only [WidePullback.lift_π, Category.assoc, ← X.left.map_comp_assoc]           rfl         · dsimp           simp }   right := G.right

CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.cechNerv.fullDefinition: def cechNerveEquiv (X : SimplicialObject.Augmented C) (F : Arrow C) :     (Augmented.toArrow.obj X ⟶ F) ≃ (X ⟶ F.augmentedCechNerve) where   toFun := equivalenceLeftToRight _ _   invFun := equivalenceRightToLeft _ _   left_inv := by     intro A     ext     · dsimp       erw [WidePullback.lift_π]       nth_rw 2 [← Category.id_comp A.left]       congr 1       convert X.left.map_id _       rw [← op_id]       congr 1       ext ⟨a, ha⟩       change a < 1 at ha       change 0 = a       omega     · rfl   right_inv := by     intro A     ext x : 2     · refine WidePullback.hom_ext _ _ _ (fun j => ?_) ?_       · dsimp         simp         rfl       · simpa using congr_app A.w.symm x     · rfl
CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.cechNerv.description: The definition establishes a correspondence between morphisms from an augmented simplicial object to an arrow and morphisms from that object to its augmented Čech nerve, facilitating the construction of the Čech adjunction.

CategoryTheory.CechNerveTerminalFrom.wid.description: The definition describes a limit cone on a wide cospan involving a product object in a category with a terminal object and finite products.

SSet.horn.edge.fullDefinition: def edge (n : ℕ) (i a b : Fin (n+1)) (hab : a ≤ b) (H : Finset.card {i, a, b} ≤ n) :     Λ[n, i] _[1] := by   refine ⟨standardSimplex.edge n a b hab, ?range⟩   case range =>     suffices ∃ x, ¬i = x ∧ ¬a = x ∧ ¬b = x by       simpa only [unop_op, SimplexCategory.len_mk, asOrderHom, SimplexCategory.Hom.toOrderHom_mk,         Set.union_singleton, ne_eq, ← Set.univ_subset_iff, Set.subset_def, Set.mem_univ,         Set.mem_insert_iff, @eq_comm _ _ i, Set.mem_range, forall_true_left, not_forall, not_or,         not_exists, Fin.forall_fin_two]     contrapose! H     replace H : univ ⊆ {i, a, b} :=       fun x _ ↦ by simpa [or_iff_not_imp_left, eq_comm] using H x     replace H := card_le_card H     rwa [card_fin] at H

explanatories.Fin.zero_le: Any finite number is greater than or equal to zero.

AlgebraicTopology.NormalizedMooreComplex.fullDefinition: def objD : ∀ n : ℕ, (objX X (n + 1) : C) ⟶ (objX X n : C)   | 0 => Subobject.arrow _ ≫ X.δ (0 : Fin 2) ≫ inv (⊤ : Subobject _).arrow   | n + 1 => by     -- The differential is `Subobject.arrow _ ≫ X.δ (0 : Fin (n+3))`,     -- factored through the intersection of the kernels.     refine factorThru _ (arrow _ ≫ X.δ (0 : Fin (n + 3))) ?_     -- We now need to show that it factors!     -- A morphism factors through an intersection of subobjects if it factors through each.     refine (finset_inf_factors _).mpr fun i _ => ?_     -- A morphism `f` factors through the kernel of `g` exactly if `f ≫ g = 0`.     apply kernelSubobject_factors     dsimp [objX]     -- Use a simplicial identity     erw [Category.assoc, ← X.δ_comp_δ (Fin.zero_le i.succ)]     -- We can rewrite the arrow out of the intersection of all the kernels as a composition     -- of a morphism we don't care about with the arrow out of the kernel of `X.δ i.succ.succ`.     rw [← factorThru_arrow _ _ (finset_inf_arrow_factors Finset.univ _ i.succ (by simp)),       Category.assoc, kernelSubobject_arrow_comp_assoc, zero_comp, comp_zero] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

AlgebraicTopology.normalizedMooreComplex.{u_1, u_2} (C : Type u_1) [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [Abelian C] :

AlgebraicTopology.normalizedMooreComplex.comment:
The (normalized) Moore complex of a simplicial object `X` in an abelian category `C`.

The `n`-th object is intersection of
the kernels of `X.δ i : X.obj n ⟶ X.obj (n-1)`, for `i = 1, ..., n`.

The differentials are induced from `X.δ 0`,
which maps each of these intersections of kernels to the next.

The differentials are induced from `X.δ 0`,
which maps each of these intersections of kernels to the next.

AlgebraicTopology.inclusionOfMooreComple.fullDefinition: def inclusionOfMooreComplexMap (X : SimplicialObject A) :     (normalizedMooreComplex A).obj X ⟶ (alternatingFaceMapComplex A).obj X := by   dsimp only [normalizedMooreComplex, NormalizedMooreComplex.obj,     alternatingFaceMapComplex, AlternatingFaceMapComplex.obj]   apply ChainComplex.ofHom _ _ _ _ _ _ (fun n => (NormalizedMooreComplex.objX X n).arrow)   /- we have to show the compatibility of the differentials on the alternating            face map complex with those defined on the normalized Moore complex:            we first get rid of the terms of the alternating sum that are obviously            zero on the normalized_Moore_complex -/   intro i   simp only [AlternatingFaceMapComplex.objD, comp_sum]   rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fintype.sum_eq_zero]   swap   · intro j     rw [NormalizedMooreComplex.objX, comp_zsmul,       ← factorThru_arrow _ _ (finset_inf_arrow_factors Finset.univ _ _ (Finset.mem_univ j)),       Category.assoc, kernelSubobject_arrow_comp, comp_zero, smul_zero]   -- finally, we study the remaining term which is induced by X.δ 0   rw [add_zero, Fin.val_zero, pow_zero, one_zsmul]   dsimp [NormalizedMooreComplex.objD, NormalizedMooreComplex.objX]   cases i <;> simp set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
AlgebraicTopology.inclusionOfMooreComple.description: The inclusion map connects the normalized Moore complex and the alternating face map complex associated with a simplicial object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sum: This theorem asserts that in a preadditive category, the composition of a morphism with a finite sum of other morphisms can be expressed as the sum of the compositions with each individual morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sum_comp: This theorem demonstrates that in a preadditive category, the sum of morphisms followed by the composition with another morphism is equal to the sum of those morphisms composed individually with the same morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying a morphism by an integer before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to multiplying the composition by the same integer.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, composing a morphism with an integer-scaled morphism is equivalent to scaling the composition of the original morphism with the other morphism by the same integer.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComp: This defines the alternating face map complex as a chain complex of objects arising from a simplicial object in a given category.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.X: This defines the components of a homological complex as a function that assigns each index to an object in the category.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.ChainComplex.ofHom: A construction for chain maps between two α-indexed chain complexes is defined by a collection of morphisms that satisfy specific commuting conditions and preserve the differential structure.
explanatories.Finset.sum_congr: If two finite sets are equal and their corresponding functions yield the same values for all elements, then the sums of those function values over the sets are also equal.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComp: This defines a morphism between alternating face map complexes corresponding to morphisms of simplicial objects in a given category.

explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingCofaceMapCo: This defines the alternating coface map complex as a cochain complex of objects derived from a cosimplicial object in a specified category.
explanatories.CochainComplex.ofHom: A constructor for chain maps between indexed cochain complexes is provided, allowing the composition of morphisms that commute with the differentials of the complexes.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.HigherFacesVanish.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [Preadditive C]
  {X : SimplicialObject C} {Y : C} {n : ℕ} (q : ℕ) (φ : Y ⟶ X _[n + 1]) : Prop
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.HigherFacesVan.comment:
A morphism `φ : Y ⟶ X _[n+1]` satisfies `HigherFacesVanish q φ`
when the compositions `φ ≫ X.δ j` are `0` for `j ≥ max 1 (n+2-q)`. When `q ≤ n+1`,
it basically means that the composition `φ ≫ X.δ j` are `0` for the `q` highest
possible values of a nonzero `j`. Otherwise, when `q ≥ n+2`, all the compositions
`φ ≫ X.δ j` for nonzero `j` vanish. See also the lemma `comp_P_eq_self_iff` in
`Projections.lean` which states that `HigherFacesVanish q φ` is equivalent to
the identity `φ ≫ (P q).f (n+1) = φ`.

explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.P: This definition provides an inductive construction of projection morphisms from a simplicial object to itself, starting with the identity morphism and recursively adding null homotopic maps.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.Hom.f: This defines a morphism between two homological complexes that assigns a morphism from the component at a given index in the first complex to the component at the same index in the second complex.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.P_succ: This theorem establishes that the projection morphism for a simplicial object at the next stage can be expressed as the composition of the previous projection and a combination of the identity morphism with a null homotopic map.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.P_zero: This theorem states that the projection morphism associated with the simplicial object at zero degree is equal to the identity morphism on the entire underlying space of the simplicial object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.alternatingFaceMapComp: This defines a functor that associates each simplicial object in a given category with a corresponding chain complex.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition with a morphism preserves the addition of morphisms.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.natTransP.fullDefinition: def natTransP (q : ℕ) : alternatingFaceMapComplex C ⟶ alternatingFaceMapComplex C where   app X := P q   naturality _ _ f := by     induction' q with q hq     · dsimp [alternatingFaceMapComplex]       simp only [P_zero, id_comp, comp_id]     · simp only [P_succ, add_comp, comp_add, assoc, comp_id, hq, reassoc_of% hq]       erw [(natTransHσ q).naturality f]       rfl set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.natTransP.description: This definition establishes that for each non-negative integer, there is a natural transformation from the alternating face map complex to itself.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.decomposition_.code:
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.decomposition_Q.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [Preadditive C]
  {X : SimplicialObject C} (n q : ℕ) :
  (Q q).f (n + 1) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.filter (fun i => ↑i < q) Finset.univ, (P ↑i).f (n + 1) ≫ X.δ i.rev.succ ≫ X.σ i.rev
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.decomposition_.comment:
In each positive degree, this lemma decomposes the idempotent endomorphism
`Q q` as a sum of morphisms which are postcompositions with suitable degeneracies.
As `Q q` is the complement projection to `P q`, this implies that in the case of
simplicial abelian groups, any $(n+1)$-simplex $x$ can be decomposed as
$x = x' + \sum (i=0}^{q-1} σ_{n-i}(y_i)$ where $x'$ is in the image of `P q` and
the $y_i$ are in degree $n$.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Isδ₀.code: AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Isδ₀ {Δ Δ' : SimplexCategory} (i : Δ' ⟶ Δ) [Mono i] : Prop
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Isδ₀.comment:
`Isδ₀ i` is a simple condition used to check whether a monomorphism `i` in
`SimplexCategory` identifies to the coface map `δ 0`.

explanatories.SimplexCategory.len: This determines the length of an object within the simplex category as a natural number.
explanatories.SimplexCategory.Hom.toOrderHom: This defines a method to obtain a monotone map from a morphism between two objects in the simplex category.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Isδ₀.fullDefinition: def Isδ₀ {Δ Δ' : SimplexCategory} (i : Δ' ⟶ Δ) [Mono i] : Prop :=   Δ.len = Δ'.len + 1 ∧ i.toOrderHom 0 ≠ 0
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Isδ₀.description: This definition specifies a property that characterizes a monomorphism within a simplex category as being equivalent to the coface map associated with the initial vertex.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.Obj.Termwise.mapMono.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [Preadditive C]
  (K : ChainComplex C ℕ) {Δ' Δ : SimplexCategory} (i : Δ' ⟶ Δ) [Mono i] : K.X Δ.len ⟶ K.X Δ'.len
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.Obj.Termwis.comment:
A monomorphism `i : Δ' ⟶ Δ` induces a morphism `K.X Δ.len ⟶ K.X Δ'.len` which
is the identity if `Δ = Δ'`, the differential on the complex `K` if `i = δ 0`, and
zero otherwise.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.Obj.Termwis.fullDefinition: def mapMono (K : ChainComplex C ℕ) {Δ' Δ : SimplexCategory} (i : Δ' ⟶ Δ) [Mono i] :     K.X Δ.len ⟶ K.X Δ'.len := by   by_cases Δ = Δ'   · exact eqToHom (by congr)   · by_cases Isδ₀ i     · exact K.d Δ.len Δ'.len     · exact 0
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.Obj.Termwis.description: This definition establishes a morphism between components of a chain complex that corresponds to a monomorphism in the simplex category, which acts as the identity when the simplices are the same, as the differential in the complex under certain conditions, and as zero otherwise.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.Obj.map.comment:
The simplicial morphism on the simplicial object `Γ₀.obj K` induced by
a morphism `Δ' → Δ` in `SimplexCategory` is defined on each summand
associated to an `A : Splitting.IndexSet Δ` in terms of the epi-mono factorisation
of `θ ≫ A.e`.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.obj.fullDefinition: def obj (K : ChainComplex C ℕ) : SimplicialObject C where   obj Δ := Obj.obj₂ K Δ   map θ := Obj.map K θ   map_id Δ := colimit.hom_ext (fun ⟨A⟩ => by     dsimp     have fac : A.e ≫ 𝟙 A.1.unop = (𝟙 Δ).unop ≫ A.e := by rw [unop_id, comp_id, id_comp]     erw [Obj.map_on_summand₀ K A fac, Obj.Termwise.mapMono_id, id_comp, comp_id]     rfl)   map_comp {Δ'' Δ' Δ} θ' θ := colimit.hom_ext (fun ⟨A⟩ => by     have fac : θ.unop ≫ θ'.unop ≫ A.e = (θ' ≫ θ).unop ≫ A.e := by rw [unop_comp, assoc]     rw [← image.fac (θ'.unop ≫ A.e), ← assoc, ←       image.fac (θ.unop ≫ factorThruImage (θ'.unop ≫ A.e)), assoc] at fac     simp only [Obj.map_on_summand₀'_assoc K A θ', Obj.map_on_summand₀' K _ θ,       Obj.Termwise.mapMono_comp_assoc, Obj.map_on_summand₀ K A fac]     rfl)

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.map.fullDefinition: def map {K K' : ChainComplex C ℕ} (f : K ⟶ K') : obj K ⟶ obj K' where   app Δ := (Γ₀.splitting K).desc Δ fun A => f.f A.1.unop.len ≫     ((Γ₀.splitting K').cofan _).inj A   naturality {Δ' Δ} θ := by     apply (Γ₀.splitting K).hom_ext'     intro A     simp only [(splitting K).ι_desc_assoc, Obj.map_on_summand'_assoc K _ θ, (splitting K).ι_desc,       assoc, Obj.map_on_summand' K' _ θ]     apply Obj.Termwise.mapMono_naturality_assoc
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.map.description: This definition describes a functor that maps morphisms between chain complexes to morphisms between their associated simplicial objects.

The functor `Γ₀' : ChainComplex C ℕ ⥤ SimplicialObject.Split C`
that induces `Γ₀ : ChainComplex C ℕ ⥤ SimplicialObject C`, which
shall be the inverse functor of the Dold-Kan equivalence for

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.N₁_iso_normali.fullDefinition: def N₁_iso_normalizedMooreComplex_comp_toKaroubi : N₁ ≅ normalizedMooreComplex A ⋙ toKaroubi _ where   hom :=     { app := fun X =>         { f := PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex X           comm := by erw [comp_id, PInfty_comp_PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex] }       naturality := fun X Y f => by         simp only [Functor.comp_map, normalizedMooreComplex_map,           PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex_naturality, Karoubi.hom_ext_iff, Karoubi.comp_f, N₁_map_f,           PInfty_comp_PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex_assoc, toKaroubi_map_f, assoc] }   inv :=     { app := fun X =>         { f := inclusionOfMooreComplexMap X           comm := by erw [inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_comp_PInfty, id_comp] }       naturality := fun X Y f => by         ext         simp only [Functor.comp_map, normalizedMooreComplex_map, Karoubi.comp_f, toKaroubi_map_f,           HomologicalComplex.comp_f, NormalizedMooreComplex.map_f,           inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_f, factorThru_arrow, N₁_map_f,           inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_comp_PInfty_assoc, AlternatingFaceMapComplex.map_f] }   hom_inv_id := by     ext X : 3     simp only [PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex_comp_inclusionOfMooreComplexMap,       NatTrans.comp_app, Karoubi.comp_f, N₁_obj_p, NatTrans.id_app, Karoubi.id_eq]   inv_hom_id := by     ext X : 3     rw [← cancel_mono (inclusionOfMooreComplexMap X)]     simp only [NatTrans.comp_app, Karoubi.comp_f, assoc, NatTrans.id_app, Karoubi.id_eq,       PInftyToNormalizedMooreComplex_comp_inclusionOfMooreComplexMap,       inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_comp_PInfty]     dsimp only [Functor.comp_obj, toKaroubi]     erw [id_comp] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi.hom_e: The theorem establishes that two morphisms between idempotent objects in a category are equal if and only if their corresponding endomorphisms yield the same result when applied.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi.comp_: The theorem asserts that the endomorphism obtained from the composition of two morphisms between idempotent objects equals the composition of their respective endomorphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Idempotents.toKaroubi_map: The theorem states that for any morphism between two objects in a category, the corresponding morphism in the associated Karoubi category remains unchanged.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.comp_f: The morphism resulting from the composition of two homological complexes preserves the structure by taking the morphism at a specific index to be the composition of the corresponding morphisms at that index.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComp: The mapping induced by a morphism between simplicial objects at a given index corresponds to applying the morphism to the simplicial object indexed by the opposite of that index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.comp_app: This statement does not provide any specific theorem or definition; therefore, it does not present any mathematical or logical assertion.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.id_app: This statement does not provide any specific theorem or definition; therefore, it does not present any mathematical or logical assertion.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi.id_eq: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism of an idempotent object is equivalent to a morphism defined by its associated endomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp_obj: This theorem states that the application of a composed functor to an object yields the same result as applying the first functor to the object and then the second functor to the result.

explanatories.Homotopy.refl: This establishes that each chain map is homotopic to itself, indicating a reflexive property in the context of homotopies.
explanatories.Homotopy.trans: The definition establishes that if two morphisms between homological complexes are homotopic to each other, then the first morphism is also homotopic to the third morphism by transitivity.
explanatories.Homotopy.ofEq: This defines a relationship stating that two equal chain maps between homological complexes are homotopic to each other.
explanatories.Homotopy.add: The definition states that if two pairs of morphisms between homological complexes are homotopic, then the sum of the first pair is homotopic to the sum of the second pair.
explanatories.Homotopy.compLeft: The definition states that if two morphisms in a homological complex are homotopic, then composing them with a third morphism on the left preserves this homotopy.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.P_succ: This theorem establishes that the projection morphism for a simplicial object at the next stage can be expressed as the composition of the previous projection and a combination of the identity morphism with a null homotopic map.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.comp_zero: This theorem states that the composition of any morphism with a zero morphism results in a zero morphism.

explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.

explanatories.Homotopy.zero: If two morphisms in homological complexes are homotopic and there is no relation between certain indices, then the corresponding component of the homotopy is zero.
explanatories.Homotopy.dNext_zero_chainComplex: The morphism defined at the initial index of a chain complex is zero, indicating that there is no nontrivial differential mapping from that index in the complex.
explanatories.Homotopy.prevD_chainComplex: The theorem states that for a given morphism between two chain complexes, the expression derived from the previous component can be expressed as the morphism from the specified index to the next component, composed with the differential morphism from the next component back to the current index.

explanatories.Homotopy.dNext_succ_chainComplex: The differential of a morphism in a chain complex at an index is expressed as the composition of the differential at the next index and the morphism from the first complex to the next component in the second complex.

explanatories.Eq.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.

explanatories.Nat.succ: This states the successor function for natural numbers, which yields the next integer by adding one to a given natural number.

explanatories.HomologicalComplex.d: This defines the morphism between two components of a homological complex based on their indices and the structure of the complex.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.d: This definition specifies a morphism representing the differentials between the nondegenerate simplices of a split simplicial object, influenced by the differentials from the alternating face map complex.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.ιSummand_comp: This theorem asserts that the composition of a specific injection from a cofan, followed by a differential and then a projection morphism onto the identity summand, equals zero when the index set for a non-degenerate simplex is not identical to the index for composition.
explanatories.ChainComplex: An α-indexed chain complex is a type of homological complex where nonzero differentials only occur between consecutive indices.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.shape: If two indices in a homological complex are not related according to the complex shape, then the morphism between them is zero.
explanatories.Fintype.sum_eq_add_sum_compl: The theorem states that the total sum of a function over a finite set equals the sum of the function's value at a specific element plus the sum of the function's values over the complement of that element in the set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition with a morphism preserves the addition of morphisms.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.Finset.mem_compl: This theorem states that an element belongs to the complement of a finite set if and only if it is not a member of the original set.
explanatories.Finset.mem_singleton: This theorem states that an element belongs to a singleton set containing a single item if and only if it is equal to that item.

SimplicialObject.Splitting.nondegComplex.fullDefinition: noncomputable def nondegComplex : ChainComplex C ℕ where   X := s.N   d := s.d   shape i j hij := by simp only [d, K[X].shape i j hij, zero_comp, comp_zero]   d_comp_d' i j k _ _ := by     simp only [d, assoc]     have eq : K[X].d i j ≫ 𝟙 (X.obj (op [j])) ≫ K[X].d j k ≫         s.πSummand (IndexSet.id (op [k])) = 0 := by       erw [id_comp, HomologicalComplex.d_comp_d_assoc, zero_comp]     rw [s.decomposition_id] at eq     classical     rw [Fintype.sum_eq_add_sum_compl (IndexSet.id (op [j])), add_comp, comp_add, assoc,       Preadditive.sum_comp, Preadditive.comp_sum, Finset.sum_eq_zero, add_zero] at eq     swap     · intro A hA       simp only [Finset.mem_compl, Finset.mem_singleton] at hA       simp only [assoc, ιSummand_comp_d_comp_πSummand_eq_zero _ _ _ _ hA, comp_zero]     rw [eq, comp_zero]
SimplicialObject.Splitting.nondegComplex.description: This definition introduces a chain complex constructed from the nondegenerate simplices of a given simplicial object that is split within a preadditive category.

simplicial_object.splitting.nondeg_compl.code:
SimplicialObject.Splitting.nondegComplex.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {X : SimplicialObject C}

simplicial_object.splitting.nondeg_compl.comment:
If `s` is a splitting of a simplicial object `X` in a preadditive category,
`s.nondegComplex` is a chain complex which is given in degree `n` by
the nondegenerate `n`-simplices of `X`.

SimplicialObject.Splitting.toKaroubiNond.code:
SimplicialObject.Splitting.toKaroubiNondegComplexIsoN₁.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {X : SimplicialObject C} (s : Splitting X) [Preadditive C] :
  (toKaroubi (ChainComplex C ℕ)).obj s.nondegComplex ≅ N₁.obj X
SimplicialObject.Splitting.toKaroubiNond.comment:
The chain complex `s.nondegComplex` attached to a splitting of a simplicial object `X`
becomes isomorphic to the normalized Moore complex `N₁.obj X` defined as a formal direct
factor in the category `Karoubi (ChainComplex C ℕ)`.

explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.πSummand: This definition describes a projection morphism onto a specific summand of a coproduct decomposition arising from a splitting of a simplicial object within a category that allows zero morphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.Finset.sum_eq_single: The theorem states that the sum of the values of a function over a finite set equals the value of the function at a specific element if all other values in the set are zero and the specific element is not part of the set, ensuring the function at that element is also zero.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.decomposition: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism on a specific object in a simplicial object can be expressed as the sum of composition products involving projection morphisms onto summands and their corresponding injections from a cofan.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.IndexSet.id: This defines the distinguished element of the index set for split simplicial objects that corresponds to the identity morphism of a given simplicial category.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.comp_zero: This theorem states that the composition of any morphism with a zero morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.Hom.f: This defines a morphism between two homological complexes that assigns a morphism from the component at a given index in the first complex to the component at the same index in the second complex.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sum_comp: This theorem demonstrates that in a preadditive category, the sum of morphisms followed by the composition with another morphism is equal to the sum of those morphisms composed individually with the same morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.PInfty_f_idem: This theorem establishes that applying a specific morphism defined by a functor at an index twice yields the same result as applying it once, demonstrating the idempotent nature of this morphism.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.PInfty_comp_π: This theorem asserts that applying a specific morphism associated with the entire simplicial object to the projection of that object on a particular summand results in the same projection morphism, establishing a form of idempotence for the projection in this context.
explanatories.Fintype.sum_eq_single: This theorem states that if a function is zero for all elements except one in a finite set, then the sum of the function over the entire set is equal to the function's value at that one element.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.πSummand_comp: This theorem states that the composition of a certain projection morphism, the injection from the cofan, and a specific morphism equals itself when applied to an index set corresponding to a single non-degenerate simplex in the context of a simplicial object splitting.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComp: This defines the alternating face map complex as a chain complex of objects arising from a simplicial object in a given category.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.d: This defines the morphism between two components of a homological complex based on their indices and the structure of the complex.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.d: This definition specifies a morphism representing the differentials between the nondegenerate simplices of a split simplicial object, influenced by the differentials from the alternating face map complex.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.Hom.comm: The composition of morphisms in two homological complexes is shown to satisfy a specific commutativity condition between their differentials.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.ιSummand_comp: This theorem asserts that the composition of a specific injection from a cofan, followed by a differential and then a projection morphism onto the identity summand, equals zero when the index set for a non-degenerate simplex is not identical to the index for composition.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.nondegComplex: This definition introduces a chain complex constructed from the nondegenerate simplices of a given simplicial object that is split within a preadditive category.
explanatories.Finset.mem_univ: This theorem asserts that every element of a finitely enumerable type is a member of the universal finite set that contains all elements of that type.
explanatories.not_true: The negation of truth corresponds exactly to falsehood, establishing a logical equivalence between these two concepts.
explanatories.IsEmpty.forall_iff: If a type is empty, then any statement that quantifies over elements of that type is equivalent to a true statement.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi.comp_: The theorem asserts that the endomorphism obtained from the composition of two morphisms between idempotent objects equals the composition of their respective endomorphisms.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.comp_f: The morphism resulting from the composition of two homological complexes preserves the structure by taking the morphism at a specific index to be the composition of the corresponding morphisms at that index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi.id_eq: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism of an idempotent object is equivalent to a morphism defined by its associated endomorphism.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Split.Hom.f: This defines a morphism between corresponding nondegenerate n-simplices of two split objects in a category for all natural numbers n.

SimplicialObject.Splitting.toKaroubiNond.fullDefinition: noncomputable def toKaroubiNondegComplexIsoN₁ :     (toKaroubi _).obj s.nondegComplex ≅ N₁.obj X where   hom :=     { f :=         { f := fun n => (s.cofan _).inj (IndexSet.id (op [n])) ≫ PInfty.f n           comm' := fun i j _ => by             dsimp             rw [assoc, assoc, assoc, πSummand_comp_cofan_inj_id_comp_PInfty_eq_PInfty,               HomologicalComplex.Hom.comm] }       comm := by         ext n         dsimp         rw [id_comp, assoc, PInfty_f_idem] }   inv :=     { f :=         { f := fun n => s.πSummand (IndexSet.id (op [n]))           comm' := fun i j _ => by             dsimp             slice_rhs 1 1 => rw [← id_comp (K[X].d i j)]             erw [s.decomposition_id]             rw [sum_comp, sum_comp, Finset.sum_eq_single (IndexSet.id (op [i])), assoc, assoc]             · intro A _ hA               simp only [assoc, s.ιSummand_comp_d_comp_πSummand_eq_zero _ _ _ hA, comp_zero]             · simp only [Finset.mem_univ, not_true, IsEmpty.forall_iff] }       comm := by         ext n         dsimp         simp only [comp_id, PInfty_comp_πSummand_id] }   hom_inv_id := by     ext n     simp only [assoc, PInfty_comp_πSummand_id, Karoubi.comp_f, HomologicalComplex.comp_f,       cofan_inj_πSummand_eq_id]     rfl   inv_hom_id := by     ext n     simp only [πSummand_comp_cofan_inj_id_comp_PInfty_eq_PInfty, Karoubi.comp_f,       HomologicalComplex.comp_f, N₁_obj_p, Karoubi.id_eq] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
SimplicialObject.Splitting.toKaroubiNond.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the chain complex associated with the nondegenerate components of a simplicial object splitting and the normalized Moore complex within a specific category.

SimplicialObject.Split.nondegComplexFunc.fullDefinition: noncomputable def nondegComplexFunctor : Split C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ where   obj S := S.s.nondegComplex   map {S₁ S₂} Φ :=     { f := Φ.f       comm' := fun i j _ => by         dsimp         erw [← cofan_inj_naturality_symm_assoc Φ (Splitting.IndexSet.id (op [i])),           ((alternatingFaceMapComplex C).map Φ.F).comm_assoc i j]         simp only [assoc]         congr 2         apply S₁.s.hom_ext'         intro A         dsimp [alternatingFaceMapComplex]         erw [cofan_inj_naturality_symm_assoc Φ A]         by_cases h : A.EqId         · dsimp at h           subst h           rw [Splitting.cofan_inj_πSummand_eq_id]           dsimp           rw [comp_id, Splitting.cofan_inj_πSummand_eq_id_assoc]         · rw [S₁.s.cofan_inj_πSummand_eq_zero_assoc _ _ (Ne.symm h),             S₂.s.cofan_inj_πSummand_eq_zero _ _ (Ne.symm h), zero_comp, comp_zero] }

explanatories.ChainComplex: An α-indexed chain complex is a type of homological complex where nonzero differentials only occur between consecutive indices.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.splitting: This definition asserts that the simplicial object associated with a chain complex is guaranteed to have a splitting due to its construction.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.nondegComplex: This definition introduces a chain complex constructed from the nondegenerate simplices of a given simplicial object that is split within a preadditive category.
explanatories.HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents: An isomorphism between two homological complexes can be constructed from isomorphisms of their individual components that are compatible with the differentials defined by their complex shape relations.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComp: The differential of the alternating face map complex at a given index is expressed as a signed sum over the face operators applied to the simplicial object at that index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sum_comp: This theorem demonstrates that in a preadditive category, the sum of morphisms followed by the composition with another morphism is equal to the sum of those morphisms composed individually with the same morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sum: This theorem asserts that in a preadditive category, the composition of a morphism with a finite sum of other morphisms can be expressed as the sum of the compositions with each individual morphism.
explanatories.Fintype.sum_eq_single: This theorem states that if a function is zero for all elements except one in a finite set, then the sum of the function over the entire set is equal to the function's value at that one element.
explanatories.Fin.val_zero: The value of the zero element in a finite structure is equal to the natural number zero.
explanatories.pow_zero: This theorem asserts that any element raised to the power of zero in a monoid equals the identity element of that monoid.
explanatories.one_zsmul: This theorem states that in a subnegative monoid, scaling an element by one results in the element itself.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.Obj.Termwis: This theorem states that the induced morphism on the chain complex corresponding to the coface map at the initial vertex relates to the differential between two consecutive components of the complex.
explanatories.SimplicialObject.Splitting.cofan_inj_πSu: This theorem establishes that the composite morphism from a cofan's injection to a specific projection morphism on a summand equates to the identity morphism on that summand within the context of a simplicial object's splitting.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying a morphism by an integer before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to multiplying the composition by the same integer.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, composing a morphism with an integer-scaled morphism is equivalent to scaling the composition of the original morphism with the other morphism by the same integer.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀.Obj.Termwis: This theorem demonstrates that under specific conditions related to the morphism's properties and the simplicity of the categories involved, the image of a chain complex map corresponding to that morphism is zero.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.zero_comp: This theorem states that composing a zero morphism with any morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.zsmul_zero: Multiplying zero by any integer results in zero within a subtraction monoid.
explanatories.SimplexCategory.len: This determines the length of an object within the simplex category as a natural number.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Isδ₀.iff: This theorem establishes an equivalence between the condition of a specific morphism being a coface map and the requirement that its index corresponds to the initial vertex in the simplex category.

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀NondegComple.fullDefinition: def Γ₀NondegComplexIso (K : ChainComplex C ℕ) : (Γ₀.splitting K).nondegComplex ≅ K :=   HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents (fun n => Iso.refl _)     (by       rintro _ n (rfl : n + 1 = _)       dsimp       simp only [id_comp, comp_id, AlternatingFaceMapComplex.obj_d_eq, Preadditive.sum_comp,         Preadditive.comp_sum]       rw [Fintype.sum_eq_single (0 : Fin (n + 2))]       · simp only [Fin.val_zero, pow_zero, one_zsmul]         erw [Γ₀.Obj.mapMono_on_summand_id_assoc, Γ₀.Obj.Termwise.mapMono_δ₀,           Splitting.cofan_inj_πSummand_eq_id, comp_id]       · intro i hi         dsimp         simp only [Preadditive.zsmul_comp, Preadditive.comp_zsmul, assoc]         erw [Γ₀.Obj.mapMono_on_summand_id_assoc, Γ₀.Obj.Termwise.mapMono_eq_zero, zero_comp,           zsmul_zero]         · intro h           replace h := congr_arg SimplexCategory.len h           change n + 1 = n at h           omega         · simpa only [Isδ₀.iff] using hi)
AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Γ₀NondegComple.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the non-degenerate complex obtained from a specific splitting of a chain complex and the original chain complex itself, highlighting a structural relationship in the context of homological algebra.

algebraic_topology.dold_kan.Γ₀_nondeg_co.fullDefinition: def Γ₀NondegComplexIso (K : ChainComplex C ℕ) : (Γ₀.splitting K).nondegComplex ≅ K :=   HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents (fun n => Iso.refl _)     (by       rintro _ n (rfl : n + 1 = _)       dsimp       simp only [id_comp, comp_id, AlternatingFaceMapComplex.obj_d_eq, Preadditive.sum_comp,         Preadditive.comp_sum]       rw [Fintype.sum_eq_single (0 : Fin (n + 2))]       · simp only [Fin.val_zero, pow_zero, one_zsmul]         erw [Γ₀.Obj.mapMono_on_summand_id_assoc, Γ₀.Obj.Termwise.mapMono_δ₀,           Splitting.cofan_inj_πSummand_eq_id, comp_id]       · intro i hi         dsimp         simp only [Preadditive.zsmul_comp, Preadditive.comp_zsmul, assoc]         erw [Γ₀.Obj.mapMono_on_summand_id_assoc, Γ₀.Obj.Termwise.mapMono_eq_zero, zero_comp,           zsmul_zero]         · intro h           replace h := congr_arg SimplexCategory.len h           change n + 1 = n at h           omega         · simpa only [Isδ₀.iff] using hi)

AlgebraicTopology.DoldKan.Compatibility.equivalenceUnitIso_hom_app.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7, u_8}

    eA.unitIso.hom.app X ≫
      eA.inverse.map (ε.hom.app X) ≫

SSet.Augmented.StandardSimplex.shiftFun.comment:
When `[HasZero X]`, the shift of a map `f : Fin n → X`
is a map `Fin (n+1) → X` which sends `0` to `0` and `i.succ` to `f i`.

explanatories.dite: This defines a dependent if-then-else mechanism that allows for conditional branching based on a proposition, where the outcome can depend on proofs of both the truth and falsehood of that proposition.
explanatories.Fin.pred: The predecessor of a nonzero finite number is obtained by referencing its position in a one-element smaller finite set.

SSet.Augmented.StandardSimplex.shiftFun.fullDefinition: def shiftFun {n : ℕ} {X : Type*} [Zero X] (f : Fin n → X) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : X :=   dite (i = 0) (fun _ => 0) fun h => f (i.pred h) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
SSet.Augmented.StandardSimplex.shiftFun.description: The definition describes a function that extends a map from a finite set of size n to a larger set of size n+1 by ensuring that a specified position is mapped to the original value while preserving the zero element.

SimplicialObject.Augmented.ExtraDegeneracy.homotopyEquiv.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] {X : SimplicialObject.Augmented C} (ed : ExtraDegeneracy X) :
  HomotopyEquiv (AlternatingFaceMapComplex.obj (drop.obj X)) ((ChainComplex.single₀ C).obj (point.obj X))
SimplicialObject.Augmented.ExtraDegenera.comment:
If `C` is a preadditive category and `X` is an augmented simplicial object
in `C` that has an extra degeneracy, then the augmentation on the alternating
face map complex of `X` is a homotopy equivalence.

explanatories.ChainComplex.fromSingle₀Equiv: Morphism from a single object chain complex concentrated in degree zero to an indexed chain complex is equivalent to morphisms from that object to the component of the chain complex in degree zero.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: The assertion that an element is equal to itself is logically equivalent to stating that a truth exists.
explanatories.Homotopy.prevD_chainComplex: The theorem states that for a given morphism between two chain complexes, the expression derived from the previous component can be expressed as the morphism from the specified index to the next component, composed with the differential morphism from the next component back to the current index.
explanatories.Homotopy.dNext_zero_chainComplex: The morphism defined at the initial index of a chain complex is zero, indicating that there is no nontrivial differential mapping from that index in the complex.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.ite_true: The theorem states that when a conditional statement checks for truth, it effectively simplifies to the first option provided in that statement.

explanatories.not_true: The negation of truth corresponds exactly to falsehood, establishing a logical equivalence between these two concepts.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComp: The differential of the alternating face map complex at a given index is expressed as a signed sum over the face operators applied to the simplicial object at that index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp: This theorem establishes that negating a morphism before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category yields the same result as negating the composition of the morphism with the second morphism.
explanatories.Fin.sum_univ_two: This theorem states that the product of the values of a function defined on a finite set with two elements is equal to the product of the values at each of those two elements.
explanatories.pow_zero: This theorem asserts that any element raised to the power of zero in a monoid equals the identity element of that monoid.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.Fin.val_one: The value of the finite number one is equal to the natural number one.
explanatories.pow_one: This theorem states that in a monoid, raising an element to the power of one yields the element itself.
explanatories.neg_smul: This theorem states that negating the scalar before multiplying by an element of a module is equivalent to negating the product of the scalar and the element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_neg: This theorem demonstrates that composing a morphism with the negation of another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to negating the composition of the first morphism with the second morphism.
explanatories.neg_add_rev: This theorem states that in a subtraction monoid, the negation of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their negations in reverse order.
explanatories.neg_neg: This theorem states that applying the negation operation twice on an element in a type with involutive negation returns the original element.
explanatories.neg_add_cancel_right: This theorem states that in an additive group, adding the inverse of an element to another element and then that element back results in the original element.
explanatories.Homotopy.dNext_succ_chainComplex: The differential of a morphism in a chain complex at an index is expressed as the composition of the differential at the next index and the morphism from the first complex to the next component in the second complex.
explanatories.Fin.sum_univ_succ: This theorem asserts that the product of a function evaluated over all elements of a finite set including an initial element can be represented as the product of that initial element and the product of the function evaluated on the subsequent elements of the set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sum_comp: This theorem demonstrates that in a preadditive category, the sum of morphisms followed by the composition with another morphism is equal to the sum of those morphisms composed individually with the same morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying a morphism by an integer before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to multiplying the composition by the same integer.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sum: This theorem asserts that in a preadditive category, the composition of a morphism with a finite sum of other morphisms can be expressed as the sum of the compositions with each individual morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, composing a morphism with an integer-scaled morphism is equivalent to scaling the composition of the original morphism with the other morphism by the same integer.
explanatories.zsmul_neg: Multiplying the negation of an element by an integer results in the negation of the product of the integer and the original element in a subtraction monoid.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.mul_neg: Multiplication of an element by the negation of another element results in the negation of the product of those two elements in an algebraic structure equipped with multiplication and distributive negation.
explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.neg_zsmul: The theorem states that negating the scalar multiplication of an element by an integer results in the same outcome as multiplying the element by the negative of that integer.
explanatories.neg_add_cancel_comm_assoc: This theorem shows that in an additive commutative group, negating an element and adding it to the sum of another element and the original element results in the other element.
explanatories.add_left_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, the sum of an element and its additive inverse equals the zero element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.zero_comp: This theorem states that composing a zero morphism with any morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.Homotopy.ofEq: This defines a relationship stating that two equal chain maps between homological complexes are homotopic to each other.

explanatories.ChainComplex.single₀: The functor constructs a chain complex that is entirely concentrated in degree zero from an object in a categorical context.
explanatories.ChainComplex.fromSingle₀Equiv: Morphism from a single object chain complex concentrated in degree zero to an indexed chain complex is equivalent to morphisms from that object to the component of the chain complex in degree zero.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: The assertion that an element is equal to itself is logically equivalent to stating that a truth exists.
explanatories.Homotopy.prevD_chainComplex: The theorem states that for a given morphism between two chain complexes, the expression derived from the previous component can be expressed as the morphism from the specified index to the next component, composed with the differential morphism from the next component back to the current index.
explanatories.Homotopy.dNext_zero_chainComplex: The morphism defined at the initial index of a chain complex is zero, indicating that there is no nontrivial differential mapping from that index in the complex.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.ite_true: The theorem states that when a conditional statement checks for truth, it effectively simplifies to the first option provided in that statement.
explanatories.ComplexShape.down_Rel: This input does not provide any theorem or mathematical statement to summarize.
explanatories.not_true: The negation of truth corresponds exactly to falsehood, establishing a logical equivalence between these two concepts.
explanatories.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComp: The differential of the alternating face map complex at a given index is expressed as a signed sum over the face operators applied to the simplicial object at that index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp: This theorem establishes that negating a morphism before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category yields the same result as negating the composition of the morphism with the second morphism.
explanatories.Fin.sum_univ_two: This theorem states that the product of the values of a function defined on a finite set with two elements is equal to the product of the values at each of those two elements.
explanatories.pow_zero: This theorem asserts that any element raised to the power of zero in a monoid equals the identity element of that monoid.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.Fin.val_one: The value of the finite number one is equal to the natural number one.
explanatories.pow_one: This theorem states that in a monoid, raising an element to the power of one yields the element itself.
explanatories.neg_smul: This theorem states that negating the scalar before multiplying by an element of a module is equivalent to negating the product of the scalar and the element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_neg: This theorem demonstrates that composing a morphism with the negation of another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to negating the composition of the first morphism with the second morphism.
explanatories.neg_add_rev: This theorem states that in a subtraction monoid, the negation of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their negations in reverse order.
explanatories.neg_neg: This theorem states that applying the negation operation twice on an element in a type with involutive negation returns the original element.
explanatories.neg_add_cancel_right: This theorem states that in an additive group, adding the inverse of an element to another element and then that element back results in the original element.
explanatories.Homotopy.dNext_succ_chainComplex: The differential of a morphism in a chain complex at an index is expressed as the composition of the differential at the next index and the morphism from the first complex to the next component in the second complex.
explanatories.Fin.sum_univ_succ: This theorem asserts that the product of a function evaluated over all elements of a finite set including an initial element can be represented as the product of that initial element and the product of the function evaluated on the subsequent elements of the set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sum_comp: This theorem demonstrates that in a preadditive category, the sum of morphisms followed by the composition with another morphism is equal to the sum of those morphisms composed individually with the same morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying a morphism by an integer before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to multiplying the composition by the same integer.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sum: This theorem asserts that in a preadditive category, the composition of a morphism with a finite sum of other morphisms can be expressed as the sum of the compositions with each individual morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, composing a morphism with an integer-scaled morphism is equivalent to scaling the composition of the original morphism with the other morphism by the same integer.
explanatories.zsmul_neg: Multiplying the negation of an element by an integer results in the negation of the product of the integer and the original element in a subtraction monoid.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.mul_neg: Multiplication of an element by the negation of another element results in the negation of the product of those two elements in an algebraic structure equipped with multiplication and distributive negation.
explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.neg_zsmul: The theorem states that negating the scalar multiplication of an element by an integer results in the same outcome as multiplying the element by the negative of that integer.
explanatories.neg_add_cancel_comm_assoc: This theorem shows that in an additive commutative group, negating an element and adding it to the sum of another element and the original element results in the other element.
explanatories.add_left_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, the sum of an element and its additive inverse equals the zero element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.zero_comp: This theorem states that composing a zero morphism with any morphism results in a zero morphism.

TopCat.toSSet.comment:
The functor associating the *singular simplicial set* to a topological space.

Let `X` be a topological space.
Then the singular simplicial set of `X`
has as `n`-simplices the continuous maps `[n].toTop → X`.
Here, `[n].toTop` is the standard topological `n`-simplex,
defined as `{ f : Fin (n+1) → ℝ≥0 // ∑ i, f i = 1 }` with its subspace topology.

Path.Homotopy.reflTransSymm.fullDefinition: def reflTransSymm (p : Path x₀ x₁) : Homotopy (Path.refl x₀) (p.trans p.symm) where   toFun x := p ⟨reflTransSymmAux x, reflTransSymmAux_mem_I x⟩   continuous_toFun := by continuity   map_zero_left := by simp [reflTransSymmAux]   map_one_left x := by     dsimp only [reflTransSymmAux, Path.coe_toContinuousMap, Path.trans]     change _ = ite _ _ _     split_ifs with h     · rw [Path.extend, Set.IccExtend_of_mem]       · norm_num       · rw [unitInterval.mul_pos_mem_iff zero_lt_two]         exact ⟨unitInterval.nonneg x, h⟩     · rw [Path.symm, Path.extend, Set.IccExtend_of_mem]       · simp only [Set.Icc.coe_one, one_mul, coe_mk_mk, Function.comp_apply]         congr 1         ext         norm_num [sub_sub_eq_add_sub]       · rw [unitInterval.two_mul_sub_one_mem_iff]         exact ⟨(not_le.1 h).le, unitInterval.le_one x⟩   prop' t x hx := by     simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.mem_insert_iff] at hx     simp only [ContinuousMap.coe_mk, coe_toContinuousMap, Path.refl_apply]     cases hx with     | inl hx     | inr hx =>       rw [hx]       norm_num [reflTransSymmAux]

explanatories.Path.map_trans: This theorem asserts that the path resulting from the composition of two paths transformed by a continuous function is equivalent to the composition of the transformed individual paths.
explanatories.Path.map_id: This theorem asserts that mapping a path using the identity function results in the original path.
explanatories.Quotient.map_mk: There is no specific theorem or definition provided, but the comments explain the concepts related to extending binary functions to work with equivalence classes in setoids and quotient types.
explanatories.Path.map_map: This theorem asserts that mapping a path through two consecutive continuous functions yields the same result as directly mapping the original path through the composition of those functions.
explanatories.Quotient.eq': The equality of two quotient representations is equivalent to the relation defined by the setoid indicating that the two original elements are equivalent.

explanatories.ContinuousMap.Homotopy.evalAt: This definition provides a way to obtain a path in the target space between the images of a point under two homotopic continuous functions, based on the point's position in the domain.

continuous_map.homotopy.eq_diag_path.description: This theorem demonstrates the relationship between paths in a topological space under a homotopy, showing that the composition of the maps associated with these paths and homotopy evaluations yields a diagonal path.

FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.homotopicMaps.fullDefinition: def homotopicMapsNatIso : @Quiver.Hom _ Functor.category.toQuiver (πₘ f) (πₘ g) where   app x := ⟦H.evalAt x.as⟧   -- Porting note: Turned `rw` into `erw` in the line below   naturality x y p := by erw [(H.eq_diag_path p).1, (H.eq_diag_path p).2]
FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.homotopicMaps.description: This defines a natural isomorphism between the functors induced by two continuous maps that are related by a homotopy.

FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomoto.comment: Homotopy equivalent topological spaces have equivalent fundamental groupoids.

explanatories.Quotient.mk: The canonical quotient map transforms an element into its associated equivalence class under a given setoid.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.mk: This theorem describes the construction of a continuous map between two topological spaces from a function and the condition that this function is continuous.
explanatories.Prod.mk: A pair is constructed from two given terms, resulting in a tuple that combines them.
explanatories.FundamentalGroupoid.mk: This theorem shows that for a given type and a specific element of that type, one can construct an instance of the fundamental groupoid associated with that type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk: This definition establishes that an equivalence between two categories can be constructed from two functors and natural isomorphisms that relate their compositions to the identity functors of each category.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.toFun: This defines a function that converts a homotopy equivalence between topological spaces into a continuous map.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.invFun: This defines a function that retrieves the inverse continuous map of a homotopy equivalence between two topological spaces.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Grpd.hom_to_functor: This theorem shows that the composition of morphisms in the category of groupoids corresponds to the composition of functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Grpd.id_to_functor: This theorem states that the identity morphism in the category of groupoids corresponds to the identity functor associated with a given groupoid.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.left_inv: This theorem states that the composition of a homotopy equivalence's inverse function with the original function is homotopic to the identity function on the source space.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id: A functor preserves identity morphisms by ensuring that the image of an identity morphism in one category is the identity morphism of the corresponding object in the mapped category.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv.right_inv: This theorem asserts that the composition of a homotopy equivalence with its inverse function is homotopic to the identity function on the target space.

FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomoto.fullDefinition: def equivOfHomotopyEquiv (hequiv : X ≃ₕ Y) : πₓ X ≌ πₓ Y := by   apply CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk (πₘ hequiv.toFun : πₓ X ⥤ πₓ Y)     (πₘ hequiv.invFun : πₓ Y ⥤ πₓ X) <;>     simp only [Grpd.hom_to_functor, Grpd.id_to_functor]   · convert (asIso (homotopicMapsNatIso hequiv.left_inv.some)).symm     exacts [((π).map_id X).symm, ((π).map_comp _ _).symm]   · convert asIso (homotopicMapsNatIso hequiv.right_inv.some)     exacts [((π).map_comp _ _).symm, ((π).map_id Y).symm]
FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomoto.description: This defines an equivalence between the fundamental groupoids of two topological spaces that are homotopy equivalent.

simply_connected_def.code:
simply_connected_def.{u_1} (X : Type u_1) [TopologicalSpace X] :
  SimplyConnectedSpace X ↔ Nonempty (FundamentalGroupoid X ≌ Discrete Unit)
simply_connected_def.description: A space is simply connected if and only if its fundamental groupoid is equivalent to the discrete groupoid with a single point.

SimplyConnectedSpace.ofContractible.code: SimplyConnectedSpace.ofContractible.{u} (Y : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Y] [ContractibleSpace Y] : SimplyConnectedSpace Y

explanatories.Nonempty.some: A nonempty type guarantees the existence of an element that can be extracted from it.
explanatories.TopCat.of: This constructs a bundled topological space from an underlying type along with its topological structure.
explanatories.FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomoto: This defines an equivalence between the fundamental groupoids of two topological spaces that are homotopy equivalent.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.trans: This definition asserts that the equivalence between categories is transitive, meaning if one category is equivalent to a second, and that second category is equivalent to a third, then the first category is also equivalent to the third.

SimplyConnectedSpace.ofContractible.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) ofContractible (Y : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Y] [ContractibleSpace Y] :     SimplyConnectedSpace Y where   equiv_unit :=     let H : TopCat.of Y ≃ₕ TopCat.of PUnit.{u+1} := (ContractibleSpace.hequiv Y PUnit.{u+1}).some     ⟨(FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomotopyEquiv H).trans       FundamentalGroupoid.punitEquivDiscretePUnit⟩
SimplyConnectedSpace.ofContractible.description: A contractible space is simply connected.

simply_connected_iff_paths_homotopic.code:
simply_connected_iff_paths_homotopic.{u_1} {Y : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace Y] :
  SimplyConnectedSpace Y ↔ PathConnectedSpace Y ∧ ∀ (x y : Y), Subsingleton (Path.Homotopic.Quotient x y)
simply_connected_iff_paths_homotopic.comment:
A space is simply connected iff it is path connected, and there is at most one path
up to homotopy between any two points.

simply_connected_iff_paths_homotopic.description: A space is simply connected if and only if it is path connected and any two paths between the same points are homotopic in a unique way.
